problem:
Let $V={R}_{1}[t],$ the vector space of real polynomials of degree at most $1,$ and let the inner product on $V$ be defined as

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1).
$$

Now consider the following elements of $V:$

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2t,\,{p}_{2}(t)=t-1,\,q(t)=4t-3
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $S=\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ given that ${p}_{1}(t)⊥{p}_{2}(t)$ with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t)}$ equals $t.$

activity_context.topic_title: Projecting Vectors Onto Subspaces in Inner Product Spaces

feedback.problem:
Let $V={R}_{1}[t],$ the vector space of real polynomials of degree at most $1,$ and let the inner product on $V$ be defined as

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1).
$$

Now consider the following elements of $V:$

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=5t,\,{p}_{2}(t)=-2t+2,\,q(t)=-t-4
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $S=\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ given that ${p}_{1}(t)⊥{p}_{2}(t)$ with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t)}$ equals $-5t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,q(t)={\text{proj}}_{{p}_{1}(t)}\,q(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{p}_{2}(t)}\,q(t).
$$

We are given that ${\text{proj}}_{{p}_{1}(t)}\,q(t)=-5t,$ so let's now find the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{p}_{2}(t)}.$ This can be computed as

$$
{\text{proj}}_{{p}_{2}(t)}\,q(t)=\frac{⟨q(t),{p}_{2}(t)⟩}{⟨{p}_{2}(t),{p}_{2}(t)⟩}\,{p}_{2}(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨q(t),{p}_{2}(t)⟩ & =q(0){p}_{2}(0)+q(1){p}_{2}(1) \\  & =(-t-4){|}_{0}\cdot (-2t+2){|}_{0}+(-t-4){|}_{1}\cdot (-2t+2){|}_{1} \\  & =(-4)\cdot 2+(-5)\cdot 0 \\  & =-8,\end{aligned}
$$

  

and

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨{p}_{2}(t),{p}_{2}(t)⟩ & ={p}_{2}(0){p}_{2}(0)+{p}_{2}(1){p}_{2}(1) \\  & =(-2t+2)^{2}{|}_{0}+(-2t+2)^{2}{|}_{1} \\  & ={2}^{2}+{0}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{p}_{2}(t)}\,q(t) & =\frac{-8}{4}\cdot (-2t+2)=4t-4.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,q(t) & ={\text{proj}}_{{p}_{1}(t)}\,q(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{p}_{2}(t)}\,q(t) \\  & =-5t+(4t-4) \\  & =-t-4.\end{aligned}
$$
